source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Housing a newly weaned sow next to a boar (so she can hear, see, and smell him) speeds up her return to heat and increases her next litter size. In smallholder trials in Indonesia, sows penned next to a boar came back into heat after an average of about 7 days and produced an average of about 5 piglets per litter, compared to roughly 18+ days and under 3 piglets per litter for sows penned 50m away from a boar. Other traditional methods farmers use to help bring a sow into heat include gently stroking her vagina with a freshly cut papaya stalk each morning for 3–5 days, spraying her pen with boar urine each morning for 3–5 days, or placing her together with other sows to create mild stress.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
